sentences.text:
The present bail application has been filed by the applicant Richa Gupta with the prayer to enlarge
her on bail in Case Crime No.412/2021, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 Indian Penal Code, Police
Station Dewa, District Barabanki.
2. Heard learned Counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the respondent/State as well as perused the record.

3. It is alleged in the prosecution case that while showing the complainant dead and claiming herself to be the daughter of the complainant, an online application was moved for succession and land of the complainant has been sold by the applicant.
Richa Gupta vs State Of U.P Thru. Addl. Prin. Secy. Lko.

4. Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that First Information Report was lodged by the complainant under misconception when he has realized that the offence has not been committed by the applicant rather by someone else, another F.I.R./Case Crime No.0567 of 2022 was lodged on 9.10.2022 against seven accused persons, a copy of which is on record.
5.
It is further submitted that the offences are triable by Magistrate.
Charge-sheet has been filed.
The applicant is a lady.
She is languishing in jail since 28.12.2022.
The applicant has no previous criminal history.
6. It is further submitted that there is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released on bail or tampering with the witnesses.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, she shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid facts as argued by the learned counsel for the applicant.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, considering the facts that the applicant is in jail since 28.12.2022; charge-sheet has been filed; the applicant is a lady; the applicant has no previous criminal history and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am prima facie satisfied that it is a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
9. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant Richa Gupta be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned in the aforementioned case crime number with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through her counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.
Richa Gupta vs State Of U.P Thru. Addl. Prin. Secy. Lko.
